families.name: Standing
families.definition: Both Athletes on their feet, whether apart, hand-fighting or tied up.

families.name: Guard
families.definition: One Athlete uses both legs between themselves and the other Athlete, who is not past them.

families.name: Half guard
families.definition: The bottom Athlete traps one of the top Athlete's legs between their own legs.

families.name: Side control
families.definition: The top Athlete is past the legs and pins the bottom Athlete's back or side to the mat without mounting.

families.name: Mount
families.definition: The top Athlete sits astride the bottom Athlete's torso, knees on the mat, with neither leg trapped.

families.name: Back
families.definition: One Athlete is behind the other with chest-to-back control.

families.name: Turtle
families.definition: One Athlete is on knees and elbows, belly to the mat, with the other attacking from on top.

families.name: Leg entanglement
families.definition: One or both Athletes control a leg with their legs for leg attacks, with no submission yet being applied.

families.name: Scramble
families.definition: Unclear, in-between moments where no named Position holds.

families.name: Submission
families.definition: One Athlete has a submission hold locked on and is working to finish it.

positions.name: Standing
positions.definition: Both Athletes on their feet, apart, hand-fighting or in a clinch tie (collar tie, underhooks, two-on-one) with no leg held.

positions.name: Standing leg attack
positions.definition: Both still standing (or the attacker on a knee) while the attacker holds one or both of the defender's legs in a single or double leg.

positions.name: Closed guard
positions.definition: The guard player's legs are wrapped around the passer's torso with the ankles crossed.

positions.name: Open guard
positions.definition: The guard player is seated or supine with both legs engaged (butterfly, X, De La Riva, shin-to-shin and similar) and the passer standing or kneeling in front, ankles not crossed.

positions.name: Double guard
positions.definition: Both Athletes are seated or supine with legs engaged and neither on top, typically after both pull guard.

positions.name: Half guard
positions.definition: The guard player traps one of the passer's legs between their legs, including knee-shield and lockdown variations, with the passer on top.

positions.name: Deep half guard
positions.definition: The guard player is underneath the passer's hips, trapping the near leg and hugging it to their chest.

positions.name: Side control
positions.definition: The pinner is past the legs, chest across the pinned Athlete's chest from the side, hips on the mat or close to it.

positions.name: North-south
positions.definition: The pinner lies chest to chest above the pinned Athlete's head, facing the opposite direction.

positions.name: Knee on belly
positions.definition: The pinner is past the legs with a knee or shin across the pinned Athlete's belly or chest and the other foot posted.

positions.name: Mount
positions.definition: The mounter sits astride the mounted Athlete's torso, both knees (or a knee and a foot, as in S-mount) on the mat and no leg trapped.

positions.name: Back control
positions.definition: On the ground, the back taker is chest to the defender's back with both hooks in, a body triangle, or a seatbelt plus one hook.

positions.name: Standing back
positions.definition: The defender is on their feet (or one knee) with the back taker behind them holding a body lock, seatbelt or hooks.

positions.name: Turtle
positions.definition: The turtled Athlete is on knees and elbows, belly down; the rider is on top or at their side without back control.

positions.name: Single-leg X / ashi garami
positions.definition: The attacker traps one of the defender's legs between theirs, one foot on the defender's same-side hip and the other leg behind the trapped thigh, neither leg crossing over it.

positions.name: Outside ashi
positions.definition: As ashi garami, but the attacker's top leg crosses over the trapped thigh to the outside of it, foot on or past the defender's same-side hip.

positions.name: Inside sankaku / saddle
positions.definition: The attacker's legs triangle around one of the defender's legs, the top leg crossing between the defender's legs towards their cross-side hip.
Facing each other, each Athlete entangles the other's same-side leg in mirror image, so both have the same attacks.

positions.name: Backside 50/50
positions.definition: A 50/50 in which the defender has turned away (belly down or hips rotated), exposing their heel while the attacker still faces them.

positions.name: Scramble
positions.definition: No named Position holds: both Athletes are moving between Positions, or the picture is unclear (see the Label Guide).

positions.name: Rear naked choke
positions.definition: From behind, the attacker's arm is around the defender's neck under the chin with the choking grip (figure-four or palm-to-palm) locked.

positions.name: Guillotine
positions.definition: From the front, the attacker encircles the defender's neck (with or without an arm in) and has the grip locked and is squeezing.

positions.name: Triangle choke
positions.definition: The attacker's legs are locked in a figure-four around the defender's neck and one arm.

positions.name: Arm triangle / d'arce
positions.definition: The attacker's arms lock around the defender's neck and one of the defender's arms (head-and-arm, d'arce, anaconda).

positions.name: Armbar
positions.definition: The attacker isolates one of the defender's arms across their hips with the legs controlling the defender's torso and works to straighten the elbow.

positions.name: Heel hook
positions.definition: From a leg entanglement, the attacker has the defender's heel isolated in an arm grip and is turning it.

positions.name: Other submission
positions.definition: Any other locked-on submission hold being worked: kimura, straight ankle lock, kneebar, toe hold, calf slicer, north-south choke and so on.

transitions.name: Takedown
transitions.definition: The Initiator brings the other Athlete from standing to the ground and lands in a controlling or neutral Position (not a guard pull).

transitions.name: Guard pull
transitions.definition: The Initiator sits or jumps from standing into a guard or a leg entanglement of their own choosing.

transitions.name: Sweep
transitions.definition: The Initiator, playing guard or half guard, reverses the other Athlete and ends on top or standing over them.

transitions.name: Pass
transitions.definition: The Initiator gets past the other Athlete's legs from guard or half guard into side control, mount, knee on belly or north-south.

transitions.name: Advance
transitions.definition: The Initiator improves their Position without a pass, sweep or back take, e.g. open guard to half guard, side control to mount.

transitions.name: Back take
transitions.definition: The Initiator gets behind the other Athlete into back control or standing back.

transitions.name: Escape
transitions.definition: The Initiator, held in an inferior Role (pinned, mounted, turtled, back defender), recovers guard, stands up or reaches a neutral Position.

transitions.name: Leg entry
transitions.definition: The Initiator enters a leg entanglement from a guard, standing or another entanglement (other than by a guard pull).

transitions.name: Submission entry
transitions.definition: The Initiator locks on a submission hold, moving into a Submission Position as its attacker.

transitions.name: Submission escape
transitions.definition: The Initiator, defending a Submission Position, frees themselves and the hold is no longer locked on.

transitions.name: Disengage
transitions.definition: The Initiator voluntarily breaks contact or stands up out of a Position they were not losing, e.g. a passer stepping back to standing.

transitions.name: Reset
transitions.definition: The referee imposes a new Position: a stand-up, an out-of-bounds restart, or a restart after a stoppage.

transitions.name: Other
transitions.definition: Any earned change of Position not covered above, including entries into and exits out of Scramble with no clearer type.
